resource.title: Block themes: flag CSS that overrides Global Styles

resource.bodyExcerpt: In a block theme, users change colors, fonts and spacing in Styles. Core prints those settings inside `:root :where(...)`, which has a specificity of `0,1,0`. Theme CSS that loads after it with the same or higher specificity wins, so the user's change doesn't show on the canvas or on the front end. Nothing tells the author or the user why. We often ran into this on themes we reviewed for WordPress.com. It styled most blocks with class rules in `style.css`, so most Styles settings had no effect.
